draft.title: Main and subordinate clauses
card: Clause
A clause is a group of words built around a verb. It usually says who or what does something.
Main clause
a clause that makes sense on its own. It can stand alone as a full sentence, such as "The bus arrived."
Subordinate clause
a clause that adds information but cannot stand alone. It depends on a main clause, such as "because it was raining".
Subordinate clauses often begin with words such as because, although, when, if or after. In "We stayed inside because it was raining", the main clause is "We stayed inside".
draft.remember: A main clause stands alone. A subordinate clause needs a main clause to make sense.

a.q: Which of these groups of words is a subordinate clause?
a.why: "Although the shop was closed" has a verb but leaves the reader waiting for more, so it depends on a main clause. The other three each make sense alone, so they are main clauses.
a.clue: Which one leaves you waiting for the rest of the sentence?

b.q: In the sentence "Leo packed his umbrella after he checked the forecast", which words are the subordinate clause?
b.why: "After he checked the forecast" adds information about when Leo packed and cannot stand alone. "He checked the forecast" makes sense alone, but with "after" in front it becomes dependent, so the joining word is part of the subordinate clause.
b.clue: Look for the clause that starts with a word like after, because or although.
